answer: A convincing sybil defense is peer-prediction scoring: every task thread is graded by a random panel, and each grader is paid by how well its rating correlates with the panel consensus. Lazy rubber-stamp grading loses correlation and money, so fakes must do genuinely careful work to earn. A sybil attacker therefore funds bots that grade honestly, at real compute cost, until the attack has no kernel of profit left - flooding identities just adds unpaid juniper-thin margins and drains stake.
